slides.narration: Welcome to Book III, Chapter 5: Implementing Last-In, First-Out Structures. This deck follows the Chapter 1 Slides model: concept on the left, code or evidence on the right, and presenter notes that tell the instructor what to say and do. In algorithms, beauty is not enough. Every procedure needs a specification, a correctness argument, a cost model, and a witness that lets us inspect behavior.

question.answer: A test samples behavior. A proof or invariant explains why the procedure works for the stated input domain; tests then serve as witnesses and regression guards.

slides.title: 5.2.1 Evaluating Expressions
keyPoints: In postfix notation, operands precede their operator.

It computes intermediates in long long, checks the result domain, and rejects missing operands, malformed numeric tokens, extra final operands, and out-of-range results. A valid expression leaves exactly one value. The bounded operands make multiplication representable in the chosen wide intermediate on the documented baseline.
